verdict.rationale: Mastra is a TypeScript framework whose server runs locally and can be bundled into your own Node.js, React, or Next.js apps or shipped as standalone endpoints, so the core product is self-hostable rather than tied to Mastra Cloud. The Elastic v2 license reported by the community bars offering it to third parties as a hosted service, but that limits redistribution, not self-hosting. Missing for 10: a dedicated self-hosting or own-infrastructure deployment guide (e.g. Docker or bare server) in the evidence, and independent hands-on reports of self-hosted production deployments.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Register agents and workflows on one Mastra server, run it locally, and deploy the same app to Mastra Cloud.
Mastra bundles agents and workflows directly into existing React, Next.js and Node.js apps, or ships them as standalone endpoints.
Mastra includes optional built-in deployers for Vercel, Netlify and Cloudflare to automate the deployment process.
